result.title: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
result.comment: Raj Saha and Ekagra Gupta contributed equally and share first authorship
result.summary: While large language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents, their safety evaluations still focus primarily on their ability to refuse harmful requests in text. We investigate whether the refusal behavior in text transfers to tool use. We construct a benchmark of 2,304 prompts across four domains, consisting of matched triplets that present the same harmful or benign request in text-only, standard tool-enabled, and adversarially framed tool-enabled settings. We then assess tool-call safety using 20 predefined forbidden actions. Testing five models of varying sizes and families, we find that requests refused in text frequently result in unsafe tool calls. Under standard tool-enabled prompting, this divergence occurs for 10-52 percent of harmful requests refused in chat. To mechanistically investigate this gap, we identify a refusal-associated direction in the residual stream of each of the five models. We find that in tool-enabled contexts, the activations along this direction decrease in four of five models. Furthermore, lower activation predicts unsafe tool calls across all five models (AUC 0.76-0.86). However, restoring the signal to the respective text-only value through activation patching only prevents a subset of unsafe calls, primarily by suppressing tool use rather than by producing safer calls. Steering along the refusal direction nearly eliminates unsafe calls only at strengths that also suppress benign tool use or degrade the output quality. Our findings indicate that the identified refusal direction contributes to whether a model acts, but only partially explains the refusal divergence. Therefore, evaluating the safety of tool-calling agents requires directly examining their actions along with their textual responses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 2,304 条配对提示，比较同一有害或良性请求在纯文本、常规工具调用与对抗性工具框架下的拒绝行为差异，并在五个模型的残差流中定位拒答相关方向，通过激活替换检验其因果作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 「线性方向探针＋激活替换部分恢复」这套判断某内部状态对最终行为因果贡献的流程，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真被答案使用及如何做贡献分配；但对象是纯文本工具调用安全，向视觉推理迁移需较多验证。
